It absolutely moves from mere productivity to profound philosophy. Consider the science writer Winfrey Gallagher.
This is an incredibly poignant story in the book. She received a terrifying advanced cancer diagnosis.

beats.narration: It was the kind of news that stops your It changes everything. But in that moment,
walking out of the hospital, she realized something powerful. She still had a choice about where to direct her attention. She decided consciously
to focus her remaining attention on the good things. watching great movies, taking long walks, having a 6:30 p.m. martini.

Instead of letting the disease completely monopolize her attention with terror and anxiety, her life, even during grueling medical treatment, became remarkably pleasant. It proves that our reality is quite literally
constructed by what we pay attention to. If you spend your day completely fractured, constantly reacting to shallow emergencies, your life will inherently feel fractured, shallow, and stressful.
But if we connect that to the work of the famous psychologist Mihali Cheeks sent Mihi,
he used this tool called the experience sampling method or ESM.
He would beat people randomly on pages throughout the day to see exactly how they felt in that given moment. And he proves something totally counterintuitive.

People are actually happier at work than they are in their unstructured free time, provided they are in a state of flow, a state of deep work where their mind is stretched to its absolute limits, accomplishing something difficult and worthwhile.

Flow generates baseline human happiness. A life lived in sustained deliberate focus is not just more economically productive, though it certainly is that. It is fundamentally a richer, more meaningful
life. The neuroscience, the economics, and the psychology all point to the exact same inescapable
conclusion. A deep life is a good life. Which brings us right back to where we started this entire journey.
We are talking about your brain, your routine, your choices. So, here is a question to take with you into your chaotic, distracted day.
What is the one wildly important goal in your life right now that is starving for your attention simply because you are too busy trying to be accessible to everyone else?
What if your fear of missing out is actually the exact thing ensuring that you miss out on your own potential?
